newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish busy day sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish busy day sharply higher.

text.p: A combination of fundamentals suggesting snappy fourth quarter economic growth accompanied by controlled inflation, plus a more constructive turn to technicals, hoisted U.S. debt futures to sizable daily gains.
Lead-month March futures shaved gains late after probing more than a point higher near midday, a feat achieved on what floor brokers said was good volume paced by dealer and fund buying.
They noted that one brokerage, likely on behalf of a fund, bought some 4,000 March futures during the ratchet up to the session's peak, which in turn prompted shorts to cover.
The contract peeked above intraday resistance at 111-18/32 before stalling, but many players now look for more upside near-term.
"Everybody's all bulled up now," said a T-bond futures floor broker. "That deflator really did it."
Debt futures fell briefly when fourth-quarter U.S. gross domestic product showed a 4.7 percent annual growth rate versus forecasts for 3.9 percent growth.
But the deflator showed a rise of only 1.4 percent compared to forecasts for 1.8, while the price index at 1.8 percent growth was below forecasts for a 2.2 percent gain.
"The bias is still higher," said another floor broker of prices. But he said the contract could struggle at 111-28/32, close to the 100-day moving average at about 111-26/32.
Another upside challenge was pegged at the 111-06/32 area, or roughly equal to a 6.75 percent cash yield.
"We need a close above there to be significant," said a third broker.

Traders waited to see how the Federal Open Market Committee leans when it meets next Tuesday and Wednesday, although Friday's tame GDP inflation components soothed some of the market's fretfulness about a possible interest rate hike.
January's Chicago purchasing managers' index had more muted effect. The index slipped to 55.9 from a revised 57.1 in December. It was forecast sticking at 57.4.
One technician said Thursday's price performance showed bullish divergence between price and stochastics in March T-bonds that pointed to a price rise next week to at least the 112-00 level.

At settlement, March T-bonds were 28/32 higher at 111-14/32, 10-year notes had gained 18/32 to 108-25/32, muni-bonds rose 28/32 to 115-08/32, June T-bills gained six bps to 94.84, and June Eurodollars rose five bps to 94.28. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
